title: Energy Requirement Calculator
desc: Resting and maintenance energy requirement from body weight, with the k factors for dogs and cats by life stage, plus expected water intake and the PU/PD threshold. Clinician reference.

meds.name: RER
meds.bodyFn:
(kg,lb)=>'RER = 70 × kg0.75 = 70 × '+R2(kg)+'0.75 = '+R2(70*Math.pow(kg,0.75))+' kcal/day
Maintenance ER = k × RER — pick the k factor below.'

meds.name: MER by k factor — dog
meds.bodyFn:
(kg,lb)=>{var r=70*Math.pow(kg,0.75);var k=[['Typical neutered pet',1.6],['Weight loss (overweight)',1.0],['Obese prone',1.4],['Weight gain (neutered)',2.0],['Weight gain (intact)',2.2]];return k.map(function(x){return x[0]+' (k='+x[1]+') → '+R2(x[1]*r)+' kcal/day';}).join('
');}
meds.note: k values from Merck and VIN. Divide the kcal/day by the diet's kcal per cup or can to get the amount to feed.

meds.name: Expected water intake — dog
meds.desc: 1 ml per kcal; PU/PD above 100 ml/kg/day
meds.bodyFn:
(kg,lb)=>'Water intake is about 1 ml per kcal.
PU/PD threshold is over 100 ml/kg/day = '+R2(kg*100)+' ml/day = '+R2(kg*100/236.6)+' cups/day.'

meds.name: RER
meds.bodyFn:
(kg,lb)=>'RER = 70 × kg0.75 = '+R2(70*Math.pow(kg,0.75))+' kcal/day
Maintenance ER = k × RER — pick the k factor below.'

meds.name: MER by k factor — cat
meds.bodyFn:
(kg,lb)=>{var r=70*Math.pow(kg,0.75);var k=[['Weight loss (overweight)',0.8],['Obese prone',1.0],['Weight gain (neutered)',1.47],['Weight gain (intact)',1.7],['Light / active working',1.6],['Typical intact pet',1.4],['Typical neutered pet',1.2],['Critical care',1.0],['Healthy kitten',2.5]];return k.map(function(x){return x[0]+' (k='+x[1]+') → '+R2(x[1]*r)+' kcal/day';}).join('
');}
meds.note: k values from Merck and VIN. Kittens are 2.5 both under and over 16 weeks on this sheet.

meds.name: Expected water intake — cat
meds.desc: 1 ml per kcal; PU/PD above 100 ml/kg/day
meds.bodyFn:
(kg,lb)=>'Water intake is about 1 ml per kcal.
PU/PD threshold is over 100 ml/kg/day = '+R2(kg*100)+' ml/day = '+R2(kg*100/236.6)+' cups/day.'

notes.Formulae: Resting energy requirement (RER) = 70 × kg^0.75. Maintenance energy requirement (MER) = k × RER, with k chosen from the tables above. k values are from Merck and VIN.
notes.Dog k factors: Typical neutered pet 1.6 · weight loss (overweight) 1.0 · obese prone 1.4 · weight gain, neutered 2.0 · weight gain, intact 2.2.
notes.Cat k factors: Weight loss (overweight) 0.8 · obese prone 1.0 · weight gain, neutered 1.47 · weight gain, intact 1.7 · light/active 1.6 · typical intact 1.4 · typical neutered 1.2 · critical care 1.0 · healthy kittens 2.5.
notes.Turning kcal into food: Divide the kcal/day by the kcal per cup or per can printed on the diet. A cup is about 236.6 ml.
notes.Water intake: Roughly 1 ml of water per kcal consumed. PU/PD is defined here as over 100 ml/kg/day.
notes.Critical care: Feed to RER (k = 1.0) in a hospitalised patient — not to maintenance. Overfeeding a critical patient is a real risk.
